memory_update.text: For node hyperscaler_ai_capex_and_compute_demand, prioritize direct demand owners MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, ORCL and CRWV before supplier names; these determine capex cadence, utilization and cloud revenue conversion.

The chokepoint is multi-timeline execution: chips, custom ASICs, memory, networking, servers, data-center shells, power, cooling and interconnection arrive on different lead times; revenue-ready compute depends on the slowest constrained link.

Second-order suppliers with highest node relevance: NVDA for accelerators/systems/networking, AVGO for custom AI ASICs and networking, ANET for AI Ethernet, DELL/SMCI for AI servers, VRT/ETN for power and cooling, DLR for data-center capacity.
Need follow-up on TSM, MU, MRVL, EQIX, CEG, GEV, PWR and NEE as adjacent supplier/regulated-asset mappings; excluded from this 15-name cap despite plausible node relevance.

Need market-pricing check in next layer: compare AI capex/backlog growth versus valuation, depreciation, free cash flow, customer concentration, and whether capex is being rewarded or penalized by investors.

node: Hyperscaler AI capex and compute demand
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the customer-side AI compute-demand node. The highest-signal names are the hyperscalers and AI clouds that directly decide capex cadence and utilization conversion, plus suppliers whose revenue depends on whether hyperscaler AI capex turns into deployed, revenue-ready compute. Key Serenity framing: high capex is not automatically positive; the research funnel should track utilization, AI revenue run-rate, cloud backlog/RPO conversion, depreciation pressure, power/cooling lead times, networking constraints, and whether custom silicon shifts value away from merchant GPUs.
